challenge.method: Before inspecting license material, I read the Software Commons Evidence Standard (policy_standard), Codex Research Protocol (policy_protocol), and SCES-1.0 research task brief (policy_task_brief). I applied Standard §§2–4 and Protocol stage 7 by reopening the exact sources, checking each binding, testing adverse interpretations, and reproducing the byte comparisons. For this claim I tested whether redistribution is the exclusive trigger, whether either notice alone suffices, and whether the condition extends to unrelated material.
challenge.results: The conjunction requires both notices. The clause covers all copies or substantial portions, so redistribution is a supported instance of the condition. The defined term Software limits its reach. The clause supplies no separate permission to republish a license representation.

limitations: Whether a particular excerpt is substantial and whether a particular work carries this grant depend on facts outside the reference form. The clause specifies no packaging method.

reasoning: In OSI record 395, content.rendered places the copyright notice immediately before the LicenseText section. Paragraph 1 defines Software and makes the grant subject to conditions. Paragraph 2 says the above copyright notice and this permission notice “shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software.” Redistributing material within that scope therefore requires both notices.
